title: Reply: heretics can mix true with false — rejecting tradition is not automatically heresy
source_text: XXIII. Respondeo, quicquid haeretici sentiunt, protinus tamen haereticum non esse. Nam haeretici possunt cum falsis dogmatibus multa vera amplecti. Itaque, licet haeretici illi, quos adversarii recensent, traditiones communi consensu rejecissent, non inde sequeretur tamen haeresin esse traditiones rejicere. Nam haeretici quidem illi fuerunt, sed non in eo quod non satis tribuebant traditionibus, verum in eo quod contra Scripturae authoritatem perversa & impia dogmata defendebant. Alioqui, si quicquid illi senserunt damnandum est, credendum non est Jesum esse Christum, & pro Christo patiendum esse, quod illi quoque admiserunt.
pass_a_gloss: I answer that whatever heretics think, it is not therefore immediately heretical. For heretics can embrace many true things along with false dogmas. Therefore, even if those heretics whom the adversaries recount had rejected traditions by common consent, it would not therefore follow that it is heresy to reject traditions. For those men were indeed heretics, but not in this, that they did not attribute enough to traditions, but in this, that against the authority of Scripture they defended perverse and impious dogmas. Otherwise, if whatever they thought is to be condemned, it is not to be believed that Jesus is the Christ, and that one must suffer for Christ, which they also admitted.
pass_b_english: Heresy is not every opinion a heretic holds.
False teachers can still affirm many truths.
Even shared rejection of traditions would not make rejecting them heresy.
They were heretics for perverting Scripture — not for under-valuing tradition; else we must also damn their confession that Jesus is Christ.
